{{Short description|Family of polynomials}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Gould polynomials''' <math>G_n</math>, <math>n\in\N</math>, are [[polynomial]]s introduced by [[Henry W. Gould]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Gould |first=H. W. |author-link=Henry W. Gould |year=1961 |title=A series transformation for finding convolution identities |journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]] |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=193-202 |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-61-02817-4}}</ref> They are defined in terms of the [[falling factorial]] by<ref>{{cite book | last=Roman | first=Steven | author-link=Steven Roman | title=The Umbral Calculus | year=1984 | publisher=[[Academic Press]] | location=[[Orlando, Florida|Orlando, FL]] | series=Pure and Applied Mathematics | volume=111 | isbn=0-12-594380-6 | mr=741185}}</ref>

:<math>G_n(x;a,b) = \frac{x}{x-an}\Big(\frac{x-an}{b}\Big)_n</math>.

They form the [[Sheffer sequence]] for <math>f(t)=e^{at}(e^{bt}-1)</math>, <math>b\neq 0</math>, which has [[generating function]]

:<math>\exp(x f^{-1}(t)) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} G_n(x;a,b)\frac{t^n}{n!}.</math>

The [[inverse function]] is given by

:<math>f^{-1}(t)=\frac{1}{b}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\binom{-(b+ak)/b}{k-1}\frac{t^k}{k}</math>.
